subject: DPA negotiation: retention/deletion & backup/DR carve-out (DocuSign path)
body:
---Message 1 (oldest)---
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jennifer Holt <j.holt@marketsoft.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood DPA proposal & retention carve-out questions

Hi Jennifer,

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion I attached our current DPA redline (Redwood_DPA_redline_v3.pdf) and a short appendix that sketches the proposed Backup/DR carve-out (Backup_DR_Appendix.docx).

Two quick asks so we can move toward execution:
- Can you confirm whether MarketSoft requires any cross-border exception for encrypted backups kept for disaster recovery (you mentioned APAC replication)? If so, please specify max retention and permitted regions.
- Do you need the carve-out to survive termination for a brief wind-down period, or should backups be deleted on the same termination timeline as production data?

Our preferred path is to land language that: permits encrypted, access-restricted backups kept only for DR for a limited retention window (we proposed 90 days), requires audit logging and limits access to a named DR ops team, and commits to deletion/crypto-key destruction after the window or upon verified customer direction. If MarketSoft wants a broader carve-out we can take it to legal for consideration, but we want to be explicit about timelines and controls.

If the high-level is acceptable, I can circulate a last redline and send the DPA to DocuSign for signature.

Thanks,
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwoodinference.com
(415) 555-0128

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_redline_v3.pdf (redline), Backup_DR_Appendix.docx (proposal)

---Message 2---
From: Jennifer Holt <j.holt@marketsoft.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: MarketSoft Legal <legal@marketsoft.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Mar 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood DPA proposal & retention carve-out questions

Karthik,

Appreciate the detailed materials. A few clarifications from our side:
- MarketSoft requires that backups used for DR may be stored in a different region than the applicable production region, but must remain encrypted at rest and in transit. We typically allow a 90-day retention window for disaster recovery snapshots unless otherwise negotiated.
- During an active termination or audit request we require the ability to request expedited restoration and availability for a short period (up to 14 days) to support e-discovery/procurement activities, after which backups must be deleted/destroyed upon our instruction.
- For cross-border copies we need confirmation that Redwood will not use subprocessors in restricted jurisdictions for backup storage without prior written consent.

On execution: Legal prefers DocuSign. Please route the final DPA to me and cc legal@marketsoft.com. Also include a short 'how we store backups' summary and a link to your SOC 2 controls page.

Thanks,
Jennifer Holt
Head of Procurement Operations
MarketSoft
j.holt@marketsoft.com

---Message 3 (internal)---
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Mar 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Redwood DPA proposal & retention carve-out questions

Karthik —

Thanks for looping us in. Quick guidance from legal/compliance and ops below. TL;DR: we can accept a narrowly-scoped backup/DR carve-out with controls and timeboxes, but we should push back on any language that allows indefinite cross-border retention or unrestricted subprocessors.

Suggested negotiation points (to include in the next redline):
1) Retention window: agree to the requested 90-day maximum for encrypted DR snapshots. Include explicit start-of-retention trigger (snapshot creation) and require customer instruction for any retention beyond 90 days.
2) Deletion/termination: require that at the end of the retention window or within 30 days of termination (customer instructs deletion), Redwood will delete snapshots and destroy associated encryption keys; we can allow a 14-day grace period for e-discovery upon customer request as MarketSoft requested.
3) Subprocessors: add a clause that Redwood will not place backup storage with subprocessors in "restricted jurisdictions" without prior written consent; provide an approved subprocessors list and commit to 30 days notice for adding services that might affect data residency.
4) Controls: reference SOC 2 controls, encryption specs (AES-256), limited DR ops access (role-based), and audit logging — include a one-page technical summary for MarketSoft to satisfy procurement.

I attached an internal redline with proposed language (Redwood_DPA_internal_redline.docx). If those changes look good to Karthik, we should send the updated DPA and the technical summary and request signature via DocuSign.

Neha / Marcus — please confirm the technical summary wording and subprocessors language by EOD so we can finalize.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwoodinference.com

---Message 4 (newest)---
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jennifer Holt <j.holt@marketsoft.com>
Cc: MarketSoft Legal <legal@marketsoft.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Mar 2026 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: Final DPA redline & DocuSign link — backup carve-out aligned

Jennifer,

Thanks for the quick turnaround and for clarifying MarketSoft's needs. Per Marissa's suggested language (attached internal redline), we've updated the DPA to:
- Allow encrypted DR snapshots retained for a maximum of 90 days;
- Permit a one-time customer-requested 14-day hold for e-discovery during termination;
- Require deletion of backups and destruction of encryption keys after the retention window or within 30 days after termination if MarketSoft requests deletion;
- Include a subprocessors clause that requires prior written consent for placements in restricted jurisdictions and a 30-day notice on new subprocessors that affect residency.

Attached: Redwood_DPA_redline_v4.pdf (final redline) and Backup_DR_Appendix.docx (updated). I also uploaded a one-page technical summary and SOC 2 reference into the Drive folder.

Please sign via DocuSign here: https://app.docusign.com/documents/ms-dpa-2026
(If legal needs any final tweaks, loop Marissa and we'll triage immediately.)

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwoodinference.com
